conventions.originals: inputs are never modified; an existing output is refused without --overwrite
conventions.output: one JSON object on stdout with --json; human lines on stderr

roles.analysis: measures media and writes a data file (no media)
roles.execution: writes a new media artifact; inputs are never modified
roles.orchestration: runs other tools in order, each verified before the next
roles.verification: checks an artifact or the environment; writes no media

tools.description: Measure a source video with ffmpeg-skill and write a timeline.json that the Remotion compositions read as props: real duration/fps/size, scene cuts, silences and the speech ranges between them, audio peaks, an optional beat grid, and captions from a file.

captions.description: SRT, WebVTT or JSON cue list to carry into the timeline (text kept as written)

chapters.description: chapter list, one `TIME TITLE` per line (YouTube's format, the same file ffmpeg-skill metadata.py --chapters writes into the container), or `source` for the chapters already in the input file; titles are kept as written

conform.description: a variable-frame-rate or HDR / BT.2020 source (or --pip camera) is first made into a constant-frame-rate, SDR BT.709 copy with ffmpeg-skill (fit.py --fps, color.py --to-sdr: tone-mapped, so the look changes) and everything is measured and drawn on that copy; the original is never modified. Without it such a source is refused

conform_fps.description: with --conform: the constant frame rate for a VFR source (default: the stream's base rate, r_frame_rate, so no frame is dropped)

conformed.description: with --conform: where the conformed copy of the source goes (default: <name>_conformed.mp4)

dry_run.description: plan only: return the commands, write nothing

highlights.description: also rank N highlight ranges (scenes.py --highlights; audio energy) for the Highlights composition

input.description: source video (or audio) file; several are joined in order first

join_transition.description: with several inputs: ffmpeg-skill join.py --transition (default none = straight cuts)

joined.description: with several inputs: where the joined source goes (default: <first>_joined.mp4)

margin.description: seconds of silence kept around speech (default 0.15)

min_silence.description: shortest gap in seconds that counts as silence (default 0.6)

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output file

pip.description: a second recording (camera) for the Pip composition: picture-in-picture over the source. The offset between the two is measured from their audio with ffmpeg-skill sync.py

pip_max_offset.description: with --pip: largest offset sync.py searches, in seconds (default 30)

pip_offset.description: with --pip: the camera starts this many seconds after the source (negative: before), instead of measuring it -- for a camera without usable audio

target.description: with --highlights: total length the picks add up to

threshold.description: silence level in dBFS for silence.py (default -35)

timeout.description: wall-clock limit per external step in seconds (default 1800)

words.description: word timings for the Karaoke and Captioned compositions: a transcription-skill transcript (schema transcription-skill/transcript/0.1, validated strictly) or whisper JSON with word timestamps; without --captions the cues are grouped from these words

tools.name: analyze

result.summary: object: duration, fps, size, scenes, silences, speech_seconds, peaks, captions, chapters, beats, tempo_bpm, highlights, clips, words, conformed (list: vfr / hdr)

tools.summary: Measure a source with ffmpeg-skill and write timeline.json (+ captions from a file).
tools.verification: every number comes from ffmpeg-skill probe/scenes/silence; a VFR or HDR source is refused, or with --conform conformed and re-measured (CFR at the asked rate, SDR BT.709) before use; warnings for rotation and odd frame rates
tools.writes: timeline.json (+ the joined source for several inputs, the conformed copy with --conform)

tools.description: Create a Remotion project wired for measured timelines: the three built-in compositions (Captioned, Jumpcut, PeakPulse), the timeline types, and pinned Remotion versions.

directory.description: new project folder (must not exist, or be empty)

dry_run.description: plan only: return the commands, write nothing

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output file

timeout.description: wall-clock limit per external step in seconds (default 1800)

tools.name: init
tools.summary: Create a Remotion project with the built-in compositions (optionally npm install).
tools.verification: refuses a non-empty folder; npm install exit status

tools.description: Render single frames of a composition as PNG -- the cheap check before a full render. Pick frames by time (--at, seconds on the composition timeline) or by frame number.

aspect.description: output shape (default: the source's own). 9:16 for Reels/TikTok/Shorts, 1:1, 4:5, 16:9

brand.description: ffmpeg-skill brand.json: its colours, caption colour, font and font file set the look (an --options file still wins key by key)

comp.description: composition id (Captioned, Jumpcut, PeakPulse, Titled, Highlights, BeatMontage, Karaoke, Pip, or yours)

dry_run.description: plan only: return the commands, write nothing

fit.description: how the source fills another shape: blur (default when the shape changes), contain (bars) or cover (crop)

font_file.description: caption font file (.ttf/.otf/.ttc/.woff2), staged into the project

no_auto_font.description: don't stage the CJK font ffmpeg-skill finds for Japanese/Chinese/Korean captions

out_dir.description: folder for the PNGs (default: next to the timeline)

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output file

project.description: Remotion project folder made by init.py

timeout.description: wall-clock limit per external step in seconds (default 1800)

width.description: output width in px (default: keep the source's short side)

tools.name: still
tools.summary: Render single frames as PNG to check the look before a full render.
tools.verification: frames must lie inside the composition; view the PNGs

tools.description: Render a composition from a measured timeline with Remotion, then verify the result with ffmpeg-skill: probe the output against the frame count, fps and size the timeline implies, and pull a contact sheet (look.py) so the picture can be checked before anything ships.

aspect.description: output shape (default: the source's own). 9:16 for Reels/TikTok/Shorts, 1:1, 4:5, 16:9

brand.description: ffmpeg-skill brand.json: its colours, caption colour, font and font file set the look (an --options file still wins key by key)

comp.description: composition id (Captioned, Jumpcut, PeakPulse, Titled, Highlights, BeatMontage, Karaoke, Pip, or one you added)

concurrency.description: parallel browser tabs: a number up to the CPU cores, or a percentage (default 100%: all cores -- about twice as fast as Remotion's own default of half the cores)

dry_run.description: plan only: return the commands, write nothing

fast.description: preview quality: half resolution, quicker encode

fit.description: how the source fills another shape: blur (default when the shape changes), contain (bars) or cover (crop)

font_file.description: caption font file (.ttf/.otf/.ttc/.woff2), staged into the project

frames.description: render only this frame range, e.g. 0-89 (inclusive)

merge_gap.description: with --sparse: graphics closer than this many seconds are drawn as one stretch (default 2)

no_auto_font.description: don't stage the CJK font ffmpeg-skill finds for Japanese/Chinese/Korean captions

options.description: JSON object of look-and-feel options (see references/timeline.md)

overlay.description: draw the graphics only as a transparent ProRes 4444 layer and composite it over the untouched source with ffmpeg-skill overlay.py (Captioned / PeakPulse, source frame only); with --keep-graphics the layer is kept for an editing app (Premiere, Resolve, Final Cut)

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output file

project.description: Remotion project folder made by init.py

sparse.description: overlay mode that draws only the frames where something shows (Captioned / Karaoke / Titled) and places each stretch at its time with ffmpeg-skill overlay.py --place: much faster on long footage with gaps between captions. Falls back to the full-length layer (and says why) when this ffmpeg-skill has no --place or the source does not start at 0

timeout.description: wall-clock limit per external step in seconds (default 1800)

width.description: output width in px (default: keep the source's short side)

tools.name: render
tools.summary: Render a composition from a timeline, verify it (frames, fps, size, audio) and write a contact sheet.
tools.verification: exact frame count / fps / size / audio against the timeline; non-zero exit on mismatch

tools.description: Turn a Remotion render into a platform deliverable with ffmpeg-skill: its delivery template (frame, loudness, codec for YouTube, Reels, TikTok, ...) and then check.py's compliance table. Without --platform it only checks the file as it is.

brand.description: ffmpeg-skill brand.json for the template (its logo, safe margins, loudness)

chapters.description: also write these chapters (`TIME TITLE` per line) into the deliverable with ffmpeg-skill metadata.py, plus the YouTube description block next to it (<name>_description.txt)

dry_run.description: plan only: return the commands, write nothing

logo.description: logo image the template places (default: the brand file's logo)

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output file

timeout.description: wall-clock limit per external step in seconds (default 1800)

tools.name: deliver

result.checks: list[{check, status, value, expected, ...}] (ffmpeg-skill check.py rows)
result.description: str|null (YouTube description block with the chapters, --chapters)

tools.summary: Run an ffmpeg-skill delivery template (YouTube, Reels, ...) and its compliance check.
tools.verification: ffmpeg-skill check.py table; non-zero exit on any FAIL row

tools.description: The whole loop in one command: measure (analyze.py) -> draw (render.py) -> deliver and check (deliver.py), each step verified before the next runs. Stops at the first failure and says which step failed.

aspect.description: output shape (default: the shape the --platform template delivers, else the source's)

brand.description: ffmpeg-skill brand.json: the look of the graphics and, on delivery, the logo

captions.description: SRT / WebVTT / JSON cues for the timeline

chapters.description: chapters (`TIME TITLE` per line, or `source`): cards in Titled and, with --platform, chapter markers in the deliverable

comp.description: composition id (Captioned, Jumpcut, PeakPulse, Titled, Highlights, BeatMontage, Karaoke, Pip, or yours)

conform.description: a variable-frame-rate or HDR source is made into a constant-frame-rate, SDR BT.709 copy with ffmpeg-skill first (analyze.py --conform; the copy goes in --out-dir) and drawn on; without it such a source is refused

dry_run.description: plan only: return the commands, write nothing

fit.description: blur (default when the shape changes), contain or cover

input.description: source video; several are joined in order (ffmpeg-skill join.py) first

options.description: JSON options file passed to the composition

out_dir.description: where the timeline, render and deliverable go (default: next to the input)

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output file

platform.description: deliver with this ffmpeg-skill template and check it

project.description: Remotion project folder made by init.py

timeout.description: wall-clock limit per external step in seconds (default 1800)

tools.name: pipeline
tools.summary: analyze -> render -> deliver in one call, stopping at the first failed step.

tools.description: Report what this machine can do: Python, Node/npm, ffmpeg-skill (and its own doctor), and -- with --project -- whether that Remotion project is installed and its version.

dry_run.description: plan only: return the commands, write nothing

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output file

timeout.description: wall-clock limit per external step in seconds (default 1800)

tools.name: doctor
tools.summary: What this machine can do: Python, Node/npm, ffmpeg-skill, ffmpeg, a project's Remotion install.
